details:
Mars Pathfinder: project details

What it is: A web-based planetary workstation for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map". The tagline is "Explore Mars. Understand the Terrain. Plan the Journey."

Problem it solves: Mars is hostile (<1% of Earth's pressure, -84°C, rover rollover above 15° slopes), and NASA data is scattered across separate archives.

Core features:

  • 2D/3D cartography: a Leaflet map linked to a Three.js globe.
  • Dual-route planner: Route A (direct) against Route B (low-slope bypass), with 4 mobility speed models and the MSL Curiosity corridor.
  • Jezero 3D elevation mesh, built from 20 m USGS CTX DEM data.
  • Survival simulator: Armstrong limit (<60 s unpressurized), cryogenic swings, radiation (0.64 mSv/day) and NASA-STD-3001 oxygen, water and calorie budgets, with no fake scores.
  • Mission intelligence and a curated raw image gallery.

Tech stack: React 19, Vite 8, Leaflet 1.9, Three.js 0.186, custom CSS, client-side indexed JSON, and 85+ passing tests.

Data sources: NASA PDS (ODE API), USGS Astrogeology (SIM 3464, SIM 3292, CTX DEM), JPL Mars Trek (MOLA, Viking MDIM 2.1), and HiRISE footprints.

Future scope: Solar shadow routing, multi-waypoint A* pathfinding, WebXR astronaut training, and an offline PWA for desert analog stations (MDRS Utah, AMADEE).

Priorities: Real Mars data, a clear split between real and simulated data, a simple professional UI, and minimal bugs.

If you meant the Wayfinder travel-planner project instead, tell me and I'll summarize that.
